did_you_know.text: Did you know? The cave of Adullam became David’s refuge, and his brothers and his entire family joined him there.
Did you know? Men in distress, in debt, and bitter in spirit gathered around David, and he became the leader of about four hundred men.
Did you know? David asked the king of Moab to protect his father and mother until he knew what God would do for him.
Did you know? The prophet Gad instructed David to leave the stronghold and return to the land of Judah, so David settled in the forest of Hereth.
Did you know? Saul appealed especially to his servants from the tribe of Benjamin, claiming that David would not give them fields, vineyards, or positions of authority as he did.
Did you know? Doeg the Edomite told Saul that he had seen David at Nob with Ahimelech the priest.
Did you know? According to Doeg, Ahimelech inquired of the Lord for David, gave him provisions, and even handed him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.
Did you know? Saul’s servants refused to kill the priests of the Lord, even though the king had ordered them to do so.
Did you know? Doeg the Edomite carried out Saul’s order and killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
Did you know? Abiathar, the son of Ahimelech, was the only one from his father’s household to escape the slaughter, and he fled to David.
